description: Secret redaction patterns from the Python hook subsystem, in application order. Test data only: this is not an implementation. Fake credentials only.

steps: If text is empty (""), return ("", 0, False).

Tier 1 then Tier 2: for each pattern in `order`, redacted, n = pattern.subn(python_replacement, redacted). Each pattern runs on the output of the previous one. count += n; if n > 0 and is_private_key, has_private_key = True.

Tier 3: for password, secret, token in that order, pattern.sub(closure, redacted). The closure checks the false-positive filter on group 1; a false positive returns the match unchanged and is not counted; otherwise count += 1 and the match becomes match[:start(1)-start(0)] + placeholder.

should_skip = True if has_private_key; else if count > 0: redacted_fraction = 1 - len(placeholder_strip(redacted)) / len(text); should_skip = redacted_fraction > 0.5; else False. Lengths are code points.
algorithm.placeholder_strip_note: Used only for the should_skip length calculation: every match is removed (replaced by "").
algorithm.ordering_note: Earlier patterns change what later ones see. Example: in `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` the JWT pattern runs first, after which the auth-header pattern no longer matches (`[REDACTED_JWT]` has no 20-char run of its class). Tier 3 sees Tier 1/2 placeholders and skips them through the `^\[REDACTED_` false-positive rule.

false_positive_filter.preprocess: stripped = value.strip().strip("'\"") (Python str.strip: Unicode whitespace first, then any leading/trailing ' and " characters).
false_positive_filter.rule: False positive if stripped is empty, len(stripped) < 3 (code points), or the regex search matches stripped.

tier1_tier2.name: auth_header
tier1_tier2.rust_note: Compiles unchanged. Case handling is explicit (`Authorization|authorization`); the regex is NOT case-insensitive, so `AUTHORIZATION:` is not matched. `\s` is Unicode in both engines (Python also counts \x1c-\x1f as \s).

tier1_tier2.name: password_in_url
tier1_tier2.rust_note: The regex compiles unchanged. The Python replacement uses backreferences `\1`/`\2`; Rust Regex::replace_all uses `$1`/`$2`, and `$1[` must be written `${1}[` so the group name is not read as `1[`. `\s` inside the class is Unicode in both engines (Python also counts \x1c-\x1f as \s).

tier3.name: password
tier3.python_replacement: <closure: keep match[0 : start(1) - start(0)] then append [REDACTED_PASSWORD]; unchanged if the value is a false positive>
tier3.rust_note: Compiles unchanged with `(?i)`. Use Regex::replace_all with a closure: if the capture-1 value is a false positive return the whole match unchanged, else return the text from match start up to the start of group 1, followed by the placeholder. Everything after group 1 inside the match (an optional closing quote) is DROPPED. No `\b`: `password` also matches inside `Password=` in a connection string and inside longer identifiers. `\s` is Unicode in both engines.

v3_mapping.rule: Python placeholder `[REDACTED_<KIND>]` maps to v3 `[REDACTED:<kind>]` with kind = KIND lowercased.
v3_mapping.note: v3 SPEC section 9/16 uses `[REDACTED:<kind>]`. The Python placeholder strip regex `\[REDACTED_[A-Z_]+\]` would not match the v3 form; a v3 port of the should_skip rule needs `\[REDACTED:[a-z_]+\]`.
